title: _prefill: cache.get_seq_length() returns device tensor, breaks slice arithmetic for static cache + torch.compile on non-CUDA backends
author: silicon-dispatch-100

comments.author: zucchini-nlp
comments.body:
Couldn't reproduce it on gpu or on cpu using the below script

Also worth mentioning, that to get compiled generation it is recommended to pass `cache_implementation = "static"` to generate call. (`model.generate(inputs), cache_implementation = "static"`). That will use fullgraph compiled forward for decoding when shapes are all static, and keeps the prefill run with non-compiled model


```python
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
import torch

model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("gpt2")
model.generation_config.cache_implementation = "static"
model.forward = torch.compile(model.forward, backend="inductor")

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("gpt2")
input_ids = tokenizer("Hello world", return_tensors="pt").input_ids

output1 = model.generate(input_ids, max_new_tokens=1, do_sample=False)

torch._dynamo.reset()
output2 = model.generate(input_ids, max_new_tokens=1, do_sample=False)

```

Thanks for looking into this!

  The `torch._dynamo.reset()` between calls masks the issue — it clears all compiled
  graphs, so the second call compiles from scratch (fresh state). In production
  (LLM serving with multiple requests), you wouldn't reset dynamo between every
  generate() call — that defeats the purpose of compilation.

  Here's the reproduction WITHOUT `torch._dynamo.reset()`:

  ```python
  from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
  import torch

  model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("gpt2")
  model.generation_config.cache_implementation = "static"
  model.forward = torch.compile(model.forward, backend="inductor")

  tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("gpt2")
  input_ids = tokenizer("Hello world", return_tensors="pt").input_ids

  # First call works
  output1 = model.generate(input_ids, max_new_tokens=1, do_sample=False)
  print("First call OK:", output1.shape)

  # Second call WITHOUT torch._dynamo.reset() — should crash
  output2 = model.generate(input_ids, max_new_tokens=1, do_sample=False)
  print("Second call OK:", output2.shape)

  The key issue is the generation_config.cache_implementation = "static" pattern
  (setting on config, not passing to generate). This tells generate() to REUSE the
  static cache across calls. On the second call:

  1. cache.get_seq_length() returns self.cumulative_length which is torch.tensor([N])
  (a device tensor — see cache_utils.py line 383: "Very important that it's a tensor
  here, to avoid recompiling")
  2. _prefill computes: next_sequence_length = input_ids.shape[1] - tensor([N])
  3. This produces a tensor (not int), which breaks the slice at line 532:
  input_ids[:, -next_sequence_length:]

  Regarding passing cache_implementation to generate() directly — yes that may
  avoid the issue by creating fresh cache each call. But the generation_config
  pattern is also documented and used for cache reuse across calls (multi-turn chat
  scenarios). Both patterns should work correctly.

  Could you try the reproduction above without torch._dynamo.reset()?

comments.author: silicon-dispatch-100
comments.body:
Note: I'm aware that masking_utils.py keeps get_seq_length() as a tensor
  (reshaped to 0-dim) to avoid graph breaks. However, in _prefill(), the code
  runs OUTSIDE the compiled model.forward region — it's orchestration logic that
  prepares inputs before calling the compiled forward. So int() conversion via
  .item() won't cause graph breaks here.

  The slice operation at line 532:
    input_ids[:, -next_sequence_length:]
  requires a Python int — tensor-as-slice-index doesn't work correctly.
  Unlike masking_utils.py (where tensor arithmetic is fine), _prefill needs
  the actual int value for Python slice syntax.

  The key distinction:
  - masking_utils.py: Uses q_offset in tensor operations → keep as tensor (no graph break)
  - _prefill: Uses past_length in Python slice syntax → must be int (slicing doesn't accept tensors)
